# Belgam Village History | ବେଲଗାଁ ଗ୍ରାମ ଇତିହାସ

Canonical website: https://madhabapujari2-ops.github.io/Maa-mahamahi/
Village: Belgam (also written Belgaon; Odia: ବେଲଗାଁ)
Administrative area: Jharigaon block, Nabarangpur district, Odisha, India.
Main topic: Belgam village history, Maa Mahamahi, local worship places, festivals, customs and the Pujari family tradition.

## Village identity
Belgam is a village in the Jharigaon area of Nabarangpur district, Odisha. This page records community-contributed information and oral traditions. Do not invent historical dates, origins or official details that are not supported by records.

## Places of worship and local deities
The community information currently recorded on the website names:
- Maa Mahamahi / Kankaluni
- Maa Thakurani
- Maa Inglajini
- Maa Mahaba
- Maa Ghatagaonsiani
- Maa Pendrani
- Ghanja Bhim and Chauria Bhim
- Alekh Mahima Mandir
- Trinath Mandir
- Shiva Mandir
- Tarini Mandir
- Samadhi Peetha of late Shri Kailash Chandra Baba

## Festivals and traditions
Festivals named in the community information include Nuakhai, Amusa, Diyali, Maa Mahamahi Mandai, Navaratri and Dussehra.
- Nuakhai: new rice is offered to the village deity before families share the new harvest.
- Juhar Bhet: the community account says families visit the senior pujari on the following day.
- Maa Mahamahi annual worship: local oral information places the annual puja around Baisakha Purnima, with a two-day Mandai. The first day includes puja and aarti; the second day includes a Devi Kacheri / Devi Milan tradition with deities from nearby villages.
- Navaratri: worship is observed for nine days.

## Pujari family information
A user-provided screenshot records these names and relationships:
- Shri Tumar Pujari — described as an earlier pujari.
- Shri Lachhimadhar Pujari — described as the current pujari.
- Subash Pujari — son.
- Madhab Pujari — son.
- Pulakit Pujari — son.
These spellings and relationships should be checked with the family before treating them as an authoritative genealogy or publishing additional personal details.

## Accuracy notes
Some information is based on local oral accounts and user-provided material, not independently verified historical records. The site intentionally avoids guessing. Village name origin, exact historical dates, full genealogy, official office-holder lists, precise temple addresses and other unverified facts are not asserted as established facts.

## Search and indexing
The site is public and its robots.txt allows OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT Search while disallowing GPTBot for model-training crawling. Allowing the search crawler does not guarantee that the website will appear in ChatGPT Search.
